subject: Final MAP sync: POC connectivity & go/no-go checklist
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rajiv Kumar <rajiv.kumar@helionhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Final MAP sync: POC connectivity & go/no-go checklist

Rajiv —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our MAP we want to lock the final connectivity and timeline items so your infra team can provision and your security/compliance folks can run a preflight ahead of the demo week. I attached a one-page MAP draft that calls out owner, dependency, and target dates.

Can you confirm the following by EOD Thursday so we can finalize the runbook?
- Confirm public IP ranges we should allow (we provided an allowlist template).
- Confirm whether you want VPC peering or private interconnect for the POC (we can support either).
- Confirm the org admin email for API key issuance and whether keys will be rotated weekly for the POC.

High-level target: POC environment available and tested by Monday 11/09 for a Wednesday 11/11 demo.

Attachments: helion-map-draft.pdf (MAP one-pager)

Thanks — I’ll loop engineering on the details once we have your answers.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
+1 415-555-0142
From: Rajiv Kumar <rajiv.kumar@helionhealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: eng@helionhealth.com
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 08:21:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Final MAP sync: POC connectivity & go/no-go checklist

Vanessa —

Thanks, and appreciated the clear one-pager. A few clarifications from my side:
1) IP allowlist — our network team needs the exact CIDR blocks you will originate from (not just single IPs). Can you provide a CSV of ranges?
2) VPC peering vs private interconnect — for this POC we prefer peering (easier to stand up), but we need to confirm routing restrictions. Do you require full route exchange?
3) API keys — we absolutely need an owner in our org for key issuance. Can you share the minimal IAM/role requirements so our security team can provision an account?

I'll start an internal ticket with eng@helionhealth.com and have them validate the peering plan.

—
Rajiv Kumar
Head of Integrations, Helion Health
rajiv.kumar@helionhealth.com
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rajiv Kumar <rajiv.kumar@helionhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Final MAP sync: POC connectivity & go/no-go checklist

Rajiv — perfect, thanks. Quick answers inline: 
1) IP allowlist: attached allowlist-template.csv with our current egress ranges. For the POC we expect 3 CIDR ranges (egress edge) and one health-check IP. We will maintain these for the duration of the trial.
2) Peering: VPC peering is fine. We do not expect full route exchange — we will request a set of specific prefixes to be routed. Neha (cc’d) will provide the exact prefixes we need announced to your VPC.
3) API keys: Minimal requirement is a service-account-like user in your org that can receive an API key (email we send the key to). No extra IAM permissions are required on your side beyond the ability to accept and store the key. If you want key rotation, we can automate weekly rotation but need the rotation contact.

I attached the MAP draft (helion-map-draft.pdf) and the allowlist template. If that looks good we’ll update the MAP owners/times and share a final DocuSign for signature.

—
Vanessa
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rajiv Kumar <rajiv.kumar@helionhealth.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Final MAP sync: POC connectivity & go/no-go checklist

Rajiv / Vanessa —

Looping in the infra details you requested. Below are the exact prefixes we will use from Redwood egress for the POC (please paste into your allowlist CSV):
- 52.201.128.0/18
- 34.72.0.0/16
- 13.248.100.0/22
- Health-check: 52.201.200.45/32

Peering notes:
- BGP sessions are optional. We recommend creating static routes for the specific prefixes above to keep the peer minimal.
- If you prefer BGP, we will provide ASN and proposed BGP neighbors in the VPC peering stub.

Attached: allowlist-template.csv (filled), vpc-peering-stub.txt (BGP/peering metadata).

Acceptance checklist for your security team (suggested):
- Confirm allowlist acceptance.
- Confirm storage plan for API key (encrypted secret store).
- Run a smoke test: ping health-check IP and a token issuance call to our sandbox key endpoint.

I’ll be available for a short call Friday to walk the eng team through the peering stub if helpful.

—
Neha Kapoor
Senior Cloud Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com
From: Rajiv Kumar <rajiv.kumar@helionhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: eng@helionhealth.com
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Final MAP sync: POC connectivity & go/no-go checklist

Neha — thanks, this is exactly what my network team needed. We will: 
- Import the CIDR ranges into our allowlist spreadsheet today.
- Stand up a peering request (static route) and confirm by Friday 11/06 EOD.
- Provide the API key owner email by Friday (sending to security@helionhealth.com).

I’ll mark the MAP as green on our side if those items complete on Friday. If we hit any blocker we’ll escalate to our CISO and loop you.

Regards —
Rajiv

[Attachment references: allowlist-template.csv (filled), vpc-peering-stub.txt]
